newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan indicates he is one-term secretary-general.
newsitem.headline: Annan indicates he is one-term secretary-general.

text.p: Kofi Annan, the U.N. secretary-general-elect, on Wednesday appeared to rule out seeking a second term in the year 2001.
Annan, a 58-year-old U.N. career official from Ghana, takes office on Jan. 1 for a five-year term.
Asked at his first news conference since his appointment whether he would run again, he said, "Hey, I have just been elected, give me a break."
Questioned again, he referred to discussions in the U.N. Security Council after the United States on Nov. 9 vetoed Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali's bid for re-election.

The council then agreed to give priority to candidates from Africa, on the grounds that if Boutros-Ghali, an Egyptian, was denied the second five-year term given his predecessors, he should at least be followed by another African.
Annan referred to discussions during the election, "the question of regional rotation and the number of terms each region should have and has had in the past."
"The historical pattern is there and it is very clear," he said. "The answer should be obvious to all of us. I do not intend to change any patterns."
Boutros-Ghali, 74, initially said he would only run for one term but changed his mind last June, provoking U.S. anger and a bruising diplomatic campaign at the United Nations.
